newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended square, after a morning surge ran out of steam at noon amid profit-taking and a weak gold price.
The market started firm as funds put money in the market and it was buoyed by a strong Wall Street on Friday night.
"We started out positively but the strength fizzled out during the day, mainly on the gold price," Johan Marais, director at Societe Generale Frankel Pollack, told Reuters.
Gold was last trading at $353.10 bid per ounce from above $355 at the open, dealers said.
Dealers said weaker London and Tokyo stocks also contributed to the weakness in local shares.
Blue chip and electronic stocks enjoyed some buying on Monday but interest dwindled as the gold price weakened.
Overall volumes were fairly high at 600 million rand but dealers said it was not much considering the increase in JSE volumes since the introduction of the electronic trading system.
The overall index lost 5.5 points to 6,777.4, the industrial index fell 2.6 points to 8,177.8 and the gold index lost 7.1 points to 1419.1.

Gencor ended flat after its shares were buoyed to a high of 19.90 after the release of its December gold quartely results. Its distributable income was up to 68.9 million rand from 57.4 in the third quarter.
Marais said a bullish report on Gencor from one of their London-based researchers which saw its share price climb well above 20 rand this year also boosted sentiment.

Sun International lost 28 cents to 300 cents, after an article in a Sunday newspaper quoted its chief executive as saying that it was experiencing problems related to the issuing of gambling licenses, dealers said.
De Beers added 25 cents to 135.25 rand, Liberty Life rose 125 cents to 119 rand and Vaal Reefs gained four rand to 312 rand.
The partial holiday on U.S. markets to celebrate Martin Luther King Day was seen on Tuesday dampening trade in golds but industrials were seen up, dealers said.
Near-dated industrial equity futures were softer on weaker world markets and the gold contract was weak on a softer bullion price.
The all-share contract stood at 6,272/79 from 6,285, the industrial contract was at 8,013/20 from 8,041 and the gold contract was at 995/1,015 from a 1,015 settlement on Friday.
